core_obligations: One inclusion and the reduction (proof lines 12428-12443): modules of the displayed cokernel form are already known to be constructible from the torsion-colimit lemma, and since constructible modules form an abelian category it suffices to produce, for a given constructible F, a surjection from a finite sum of j_{U_i!}Lambda_{U_i}.

Produce the surjection (proof lines 12444-12460): the modules-on-sites lemma represents F as a filtered colimit of constructible submodules, and over a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme each of these admits a surjection from a finite sum of extensions by zero of Lambda; assembling these gives the required surjection onto F.

Conclude both claims (proof lines 12461-12468): the abelian structure of the constructible category makes F the cokernel of a map between such finite sums, which is the stated description, and the spectrality/topology inputs allow the objects U_i and V_j to be chosen affine.
proof_roadmap: Use the torsion-colimit lemma for one inclusion and reduce the other to producing a surjection onto a given constructible module.
Get the surjection from the filtered-colimit description and the modules-on-sites representation by finite sums of extensions by zero.
Appeal to abelianness for the cokernel description and to spectrality to make the objects affine.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the constructible sheaves of Lambda-modules on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with the cokernels of maps between finite sums of extensions by zero of the constant sheaf (statement lines 12411-12425). The proof (proof lines 12427-12468) uses the torsion-colimit lemma for one inclusion, reduces the other to a surjection onto a given constructible module obtained from the filtered-colimit description and the modules-on-sites representation, and invokes abelianness for the cokernel form and spectrality for the affineness refinement. H2: one reduction plus two standard inputs, written out.
